newsitem.title: UK: Ivory&Sime loses contract after departures.
newsitem.headline: Ivory&Sime loses contract after departures.

text.p: Fund management firm Ivory & Sime Plc said on Thursday it would lose about 460 million stg in funds under management following a decision by BAA Plc's Pension Scheme to terminate its contract.
A source close to the pension scheme told Reuters the decision to terminate was linked to a spate of resignations at I&S earlier in the year.
He said I&S was a comparatively small house, and was managing a significant portion of the BAA scheme's assets of some 1.3 billion stg.
"That and the reports about staff changes were taken into account in making the decision," the source said, adding that its funds at I&S had been managed by some of the managers that had since left.
The management contract was being moved to Mercury Asset Management. Fidelity and Natwest are the scheme's other fund managers.
I&S said in a statement funds under management including the BAA funds totalled 3.8 billion pounds.
During the year to April 30, 1996, the gross revenues arising from the management of the BAA Scheme equated to 5.5 percent of total gross revenues of 17.3 million sterling.

"It is very disappointing to lose a client of this stature, particularly when Ivory & Sime has delivered outstanding investment performance over both the short and the longer term," I&S chairman David Kinloch said in a statement.
BAA Pension Scheme group pensions manager Eric Hunt said I&S had delivered a 21.8 percent return for the scheme last year through a UK equity portfolio.
Several senior fund managers resigned from Ivory & Sime in recent months, followed by managing director Colin Hook who resigned at the start of February.
The company has since announced a number of new appointments to fill the gaps caused by the resignations.
